title: Exact minimum-bit allocation for a fixed dyadic error budget
body:
This algorithm minimizes total added fractional bits for fixed rational error weights and equal cost per bit. The executable allocator uses diminishing marginal gains; the proof gives optimality at every total bit count. The package includes a counterexample to extending the rule to unequal bit prices. The complete kappa calculation is unchanged.

[Proof and scope](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bdde72b434826be469fed1f597b838674b13b9f8/research/dyadic-bit-allocation/README.md), [exact checker](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bdde72b434826be469fed1f597b838674b13b9f8/research/dyadic-bit-allocation/verify.py), [replay declaration](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bdde72b434826be469fed1f597b838674b13b9f8/research/dyadic-bit-allocation/VERIFY.json), and [source provenance](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bdde72b434826be469fed1f597b838674b13b9f8/research/dyadic-bit-allocation/SOURCES.json) are pinned to the reviewed commit. Base: canonical main `ff3cc58e370d0f678e529246f8c73e8094e18fcf`, priority revision 7.

The initial proof and standalone check are in [Discussion #5293](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5293).

CPython 3.12.14 registered normal and optimized replays passed: 480 allocation instances, 13,565 exhaustive allocations, five input controls and an unequal-price counterexample. Both print `PASS_DYADIC_BIT_ALLOCATION`; the launcher prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. All five package files match their committed bytes, and the base is an ancestor of the package commit.

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/dyadic-bit-allocation
```

Use Python 3.12 and the standard library. No external runtime inputs or third-party Python packages are required. Hosted CI has not yet been checked. No predecessor scientific suite, selected cold replay, native replay, compiler, Lean or Docker build was run. The optional full-history preflight is unavailable in this shallow checkout. Finite checks corroborate the written proof; they do not constitute independent human or proof-kernel acceptance.

Bind fixed error weights and real bit prices to one emitted circuit. Source preparation, native operations, precision, movement, and supplier/outer admission remain separate obligations.

**Sources, limits and next step.** Credit ywz65's [PR #2701](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2701) and its [pinned noise contract](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/ff3cc58e370d0f678e529246f8c73e8094e18fcf/research/simultaneous-gate-rounding/README.md), Vlado Vojdanovski's [PR #1673](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1673), and Nick Petalas's separate [PR #5153](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5153) endpoint refinement. The greedy argument is a classical separable diminishing-return allocation method; the contribution is this exact, executable dyadic precision contract and its boundary controls, not a new general greedy theorem.

Prepared by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.
